summary: sendMail() now fails a message whose deduped envelope (To, Cc and Bcc together) has more than 100000 recipients: the new maxRecipients option defaults to 100000 (0 or Infinity lifts it), where before there was no cap
The minimum Node.js version rises from 6 to 20 (engines.node >=20.0.0) with the move to a TypeScript-built dual ESM/CommonJS package

nodemailer ships its own TypeScript declarations, which take precedence over @types/nodemailer; 10.0.1 and 10.0.11 restored most of the @types layout (namespaces such as Mail.Options, SMTPTransport.Options), but internal underscore members are not declared and some types are stricter than the community typings

SMTP server replies are capped by the new maxResponseSize option, 1 MB by default: a server reply (or unterminated line) larger than that drops the connection with an EPROTOCOL error, where before the client buffered without limit

Pooled transports stop requeueing a message whose connection closed while sending after maxRequeues attempts, which now defaults to 5 (before: unlimited when unset), and retry with exponential backoff (50 ms doubling to 2 s) instead of immediately
Content fetched from a URL (attachment or alternative href) now has a default 60 s inactivity timeout and a 64 MB response size limit, where before neither was bounded
When requireTLS is set together with ignoreTLS or opportunisticTLS, requireTLS now wins (the connection must upgrade to TLS) instead of the combination silently resolving to plaintext
Pooled SMTP connections that sit idle are closed after 4 minutes by default (new idleTimeout option), where before an idle pooled connection stayed open until the server dropped it

connectionTimeout now bounds the whole session setup (DNS lookup, proxy handshake, TCP, TLS, greeting and STARTTLS) instead of only the TCP connect, and the STARTTLS handshake also times out after greetingTimeout; a server that pauses before its greeting longer than connectionTimeout now fails with ETIMEDOUT (timeoutType GREETING_TIMEOUT)
With opportunisticTLS, when the server refuses STARTTLS the client continues in plaintext but no longer authenticates on the unencrypted connection (AUTH stays disabled)
When the server advertises PIPELINING, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO and DATA are sent in one batch (RFC 2920) instead of one command per round trip
SMTP sockets enable TCP keepalive after 30 s of idle time and run with Nagle off (noDelay), and a socket the server never closes is destroyed after close()
SMTPConnection emits only 'end', not an ECONNECTION 'error', when the server closes an idle connection or sends an idle 421

Any 421 reply now ends the SMTP session: the command gets its own error (EAUTH, EENVELOPE, …), queued replies are not waited for and the message in flight fails once, where before a server that answered 421 but kept the socket open left the send waiting until the socket timeout

A host with several addresses is connected to with happy eyeballs / net.connect autoSelectFamily, each address getting a share of connectionTimeout, and a failed TLS handshake no longer moves on to the next address
In a pooled transport a message the server rejects is followed by RSET and the connection is kept for the next message
In a pooled transport a message whose reused connection was dropped by the server before any of it was sent is requeued instead of failed

A content stream (attachment, html, raw) that is destroyed without an error, or was already read, now fails the send, where before the send waited forever or went out with an empty attachment; a failed send now releases the files and HTTP requests it was reading
The sendmail transport reports the process exit code instead of EPIPE, and a sendmail process that exits (even with 0) before the message was written, or is killed by a signal, is now an error

A per-message auth object passed to sendMail() may set only credential fields (type, user, pass, accessToken, refreshToken, expires); accessUrl, clientId, clientSecret and the other OAuth2/transport settings are taken from the transport only and are ignored at message level
Fetching URL content gets an overall maxTime deadline for the whole request including redirects, two minutes by default, on top of the 10.0.12 inactivity timeout
The DKIM body cache file (cacheDir) is created with mode 0600 instead of the process default

addressparser no longer caps nested address groups: members past 50 levels of nesting (10 in 10.1.4 and 10.1.5) used to be dropped, now groups are read in one pass and no members are dropped at any depth
